summary.name: Wazo Platform
summary.one_liner: Wazo Platform is an open source, API-first IP telephony (IPBX) platform built on Asterisk for building programmable telecom infrastructure.
use_cases: build a custom business phone system
integrate telephony into web or mobile apps
add speech to text or sentiment analysis to calls
connect call billing to telecom infrastructure
summary.what_it_does: Wazo Platform is an open source project for building IP communication infrastructure, with features such as audio and video calls, chat, call centers, conferences and voicemail. Its building blocks are Python micro-services, and all APIs are described with OpenAPI specifications. Programmable interfaces include WebRTC, REST API, WebSockets and Webhooks, intended for web and mobile use. The platform is organized into application, business, engine and technical layers, using components such as Asterisk, Kamailio, rtpengine, nginx, RabbitMQ and PostgreSQL. It can be deployed on bare metal, virtual machines or containers.
notable: API-first design with micro-services in Python and OpenAPI specs
Built on Asterisk with Kamailio and rtpengine in the engine layer
Programmable interfaces: WebRTC, REST API, WebSockets, Webhooks
Licensed GPL-3.0 with source changes required to be shared
caveats: Modifications including GPL-licensed code must be made available under the GPL with build and install instructions
Page does not list specific mobile platforms beyond SDK mention; mobile support is described only as 'mobile friendly'
